text:
sophie: Quick thread — UX for saving per-route/per-model views. We're getting repeated support tickets where saved views don't reflect routing/pin, and apps land on unexpected models. Need guidance on surface requirements.

michael: Yeah, seen that. Users assume save = freeze model. Currently our savedview only stores query + filters. No routing hint.

tara: Proposal: saved view object should include `route_id`, `pinned_model` (nullable), `routing_policy_id`, and optional `quota_preview_snapshot`. UI shows these as badges in the list.

sophie: I like that. Two practical asks: 1) cost/quotas preview inline in save modal, 2) explicit fallback policy shown so teams know what happens when pinned model is unavailable.

raj: Routing API can return a preview: `/v1/routes/:id/preview?include=quota,models,policy` — it'd return `effective_model`, `pinned_model` if set, and a simple `cost_estimate` number. We can expand contract.

michael: Small naming nit: prefer `pinned_model` and `effective_model` fields rather than `model_pin` and `current_model`. More explicit. Also we should bump API version when adding `quota_preview_snapshot` to avoid client breakage.

tara: UX question: when a user saves a view that is cross-route (e.g., top-level filter across several routes), do we allow pinning multiple routes? My vote: disallow multi-route pins — only per-route pins, show a warning.

sophie: Agreed. Multi-route savedviews can store an array of allowed routes but pin only if single route selected. Show clear tooltip: "Model pin applies only when route=X."

raj: Implementation detail: routing-service stores pin references by route+namespace. Fallbacks are configured per-deployment, so `effective_model` in preview considers the caller's deployment. We'll need to include `scope` in the saved view (hosted/dedicated/private).

michael: Also add a `save_as_canary` boolean so teams can create a canary savedview that only applies to X% of traffic. Backend-side we can wire that to smart routing.

tara: Telemetry: we should tag requests with `saved_view_id` and `saved_view_owner` for traces. Sampling: default 1% but 100% for owner/org admins when they test. That helps debug regressions.

raj: Agree. We'll add an opt-in sample override for the owner on the routing-api: `?sample_override=100`. Need audit logging too.

michael: One more: attach `eval_set_id` optional to savedview so Optimize can run scheduled regressions on that view's query set. Adds end-to-end guardrails for quality.

sophie: UX text for list item: "bound to route · pinned model · est $/day" — small, clickable to open route-preview modal. That should reduce support noise.

tara: Edge case: when `pinned_model` is quantized/variant-specific (e.g., q4_0 vs q8_0), show variant badge. Users have been surprised when pin points to a cheaper quantized variant.

michael: Good point — add `model_variant` string (nullable) and display it. Also we should have a migration plan for existing savedviews (backfill `route_id` if context available).

raj: Backend work: routing-api v2 will return the full preview payload. I'll surface an OpenAPI diff and a sample response. Example snippet:```json
{
  "route_id": "route_123",
  "pinned_model": "redwood/ao-13b",
  "effective_model": "redwood/ao-13b-q4",
  "model_variant": "q4_0",
  "quota_estimate_daily_cents": 1200
}
```

devex-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-api/v2 -> staging on 2024-11-13 03:00 UTC (rolling)

sophie: Thanks @raj. Action items: Michael -> draft OpenAPI diff; Tara -> small UX mocks for save modal + list badges; Raj -> sample payload + migration notes. Can everyone respond with blockers by EOD? :thumbsup:
